title: Composition and slice localization of projection-defined completed coefficient maps
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, its valuation ring $R=\mathcal O_E$ and a uniformizer $t$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. For every scheme $T$ use its small pro-etale site [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], the constant ring sheaves $C_{n,T}=(R/t^n)_T$, and $B_T=\varprojlim_{n\geq1}C_{n,T}$ with projections $\pi_{T,n}$ [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients]. For a scheme morphism $g:T\to W$ [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties], let $g^{-1}$ and $c^g_{R/t^n}$ be the inverse image and constant-section maps [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image]. Give it the structural ring map $c_g:g^{-1}B_W\to B_T$ characterized by $\pi_{T,n}c_g=c^g_{R/t^n}g^{-1}(\pi_{W,n})$.

For composable maps $T\xrightarrow h W\xrightarrow k Z$, under the canonical inverse-image compositor $\alpha_{h,k}:(kh)^{-1}\cong h^{-1}k^{-1}$, the structural ring maps obey
$$c_{kh}=c_h\,h^{-1}(c_k)\,\alpha_{h,k,B_Z},\qquad
\pi_{T,n}c_hh^{-1}(c_k)\alpha_{h,k,B_Z}=c^{kh}_{R/t^n}(kh)^{-1}(\pi_{Z,n})\quad(n\geq1).$$
Consequently, the two coefficient maps for any equal composites of scheme maps coincide under the specified geometric inverse-image comparison, including every finite projection.

For a morphism $g:T\to W$ and an object $u:U\to W$ of $W_{\mathrm{proet}}$, put $V=T\times_W U$ and $v:V\to U$. Under the canonical equivalences $U_{\mathrm{proet}}\simeq W_{\mathrm{proet}}/U$ and $V_{\mathrm{proet}}\simeq T_{\mathrm{proet}}/V$, the restricted rings $C_{n,W}|_U$, $B_W|_U$, and their projections identify respectively with $C_{n,U}$, $B_U$, and $\pi_{U,n}$; similarly on $V$. Restriction is the slice restriction of [def-pur-localized-ringed-site]. The constant-ring identifications are the identity on all constant sections. Write $j_U^{-1},j_V^{-1}$ for these two restriction functors and $g_U$ for the localized ringed-site morphism for $g$. With these identifications, $g_U$ is canonically the ringed morphism for $v$, with inverse-image comparison $(g_U)^{-1}j_U^{-1}\cong j_V^{-1}g^{-1}$ and structural ring map exactly $c_v$ at every finite projection. No flatness or invertibility of $c_g$ is a hypothesis.

proof.text: For each $g:T\to W$ put $A_n=R/t^n$. The constant-section construction [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image] is natural in a ring homomorphism $A_{n+1}\to A_n$: both composites send each constant section $a$ to its reduction, so uniqueness of the sheaf extension makes them equal. Thus $d_n=c^g_{A_n}g^{-1}(\pi_{W,n})$ is a compatible cone with vertex $g^{-1}B_W$. The limit universal property [def-pur-sheaf-inverse-limit] gives the unique $c_g$ with these projections. This uses a limit in the target site, not preservation of an infinite limit by $g^{-1}$.

proof.text: Use naturality of the constant-section adjunct in an arbitrary ring homomorphism, proved by sheafification uniqueness. The same calculation on constant sections identifies direct-image composition, and its adjunction mate gives constant-ring composition in the independent coefficient universe. Substitute the two completed-map projection equations and naturality of the compositor, then cancel the jointly monic limit projections. No finiteness of the quotient ring is needed.

proof.text: Use the recorded sliceFrom/sliceDense identification of weakly etale localization [lem-weil-proetale-weakly-etale-localization]. Its restriction [def-pur-localized-ringed-site] is definitionally precomposition with Over.map for the weakly etale object. This functor is continuous and cocontinuous. Mathlib pushforwardContinuousSheafificationCompatibility therefore identifies each restricted constant ring with the same constant ring on U, and its unit equation identifies every constant section. Naturality of this comparison in the coefficient ring gives compatibility with all quotient reductions. Precomposition preserves the inverse sequence limit [def-pur-sheaf-inverse-limit]; preservesLimitIso and the natural quotient-diagram isomorphism give the completed ring isomorphism and its projection equations. Forgetting commutativity is fully faithful, so the construction and projection equations lift to commutative ring sheaves. Repeat for the base-changed object V.

proof.text: Let j_U and j_V be the postcomposition functors for U->W and V->T. Their postcomposition/base-change adjunctions induce sheaf adjunctions whose left adjoints are the restriction functors. The fibre-product associativity comparisons for the equal composites v followed by U->W and V->T followed by g give an invertible square of the right adjoints. Take its inverse mate along the restriction adjunctions to obtain beta. On each H->U, the unit and counit are the pullback projections and lifts; pullback hom-ext identifies beta exactly with restriction along H x_U V isomorphic to H x_W T. Thus beta is invertible. Take its inverse mate along the recorded g and v inverse-image adjunctions [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image] to obtain lambda. Mathlib iterated_mateEquiv_conjugateEquiv_symm identifies this second mate with the conjugate of the original invertible square, so lambda is invertible. Its explicit component is the required unit/beta/counit formula. Applying the hom equivalence to the finite constant-ring square, the constant-section unit equations and naturality along the fibre-product comparison identify both adjuncts. Hence the finite structural maps commute with lambda. Naturality at every quotient projection and the completed restriction projection equations now give the requested finite completed-map equation. Joint uniqueness of limit projections [def-pur-sheaf-inverse-limit] gives the completed structural-map equality. No flatness or invertibility assumption on a structural coefficient map enters.
